en: A tired man stands by the roadside. He seems distracted by something.
The floor around the magic circle has practically been turned to charcoal. The damage is severe, but does not seem to be recent.
The man picks up his satchel and hefts it over his shoulder. Something falls off of his robes as he leaves.
There is a small bag of coins stashed underneath the bed.
This must belong to the man standing there. Best to leave it alone.
It might open with another attempt.
The lid finally gives, and the chest opens.
The lid of this chest has been practically fused shut due to decades of moisture and neglect.
Shifting around these long forgotten remains, you find a handful of old coins.
The chest is empty, and has been sitting unused long enough to have collected a thick layer of dust.
The empty chest is rotting and has started to grow some questionable mushrooms.
The empty wooden chest has started to rot from exposure to the elements.
There are ruins of long-abandoned buildings and disused roads surrounding you, but the sounds of muffled voices from somewhere nearby suggest that you are no longer alone here.
This is where you were drawn into the ghostly ruined town, and where you returned when you escaped it. You may be able to return if you stay the night here.

While making your way through the dense forest, you come across a long abandoned campfire in a tiny clearing. Night is approaching quickly and the path is difficult to find, so you decide to rest here until dawn.
While on fire watch, you nod off for what must have been only an instant, but when you jolt awake, you find that the trees have receded. Your party sits in the middle of an ancient plaza.
You find copious amounts of cobwebs among these ancient remains, but not much else.
You kindle the campfire in order to brighten the area a bit more.
Inside the water bath you see some unwashed cutlery, kitchenware, and tableware.
Rifling through the soft cushions, you discover a plain-looking key hidden underneath.
The tableware has been meticulously cleaned, so much so that you can see your reflection in each piece.
A corner juts out from beneath this stone. Giving it a little push, you find a small wooden coffer buried in the dirt.
It looks like this journal holds records for the activities of whoever worked here.
On the top of this table, someone has scratched the phrase "I hate stupid girls".
The box contains eight separate and carefully-wrapped parcels, each with a measured-out amount of gold in them. These must be the school funds mentioned in the work journal.
There is an old journal in this night table. Some of the entries are still legible. Would you like to read it?
This chest has several different sized bits of cheap tin armour, evidently sized for children. It all looks very well-used.
This crumbling chest has a dozen or more lightweight wooden practice weapons, evidently as children's toys.
It reads : Entry is reserved for the bravest of souls.
The chunk of slag you are carrying comes to mind. Will you place the Guardian Soul upon the pedestal?
The pedestal is hot to the touch. There is an inscription on the very top.
You decide to hold on to the Guardian Soul for now. Perhaps it can be of use elsewhere.
You make an offering of the Guardian Soul, a bit of slag forged from the destruction of many weapons.
The smell is reminiscent of the fluid you found when you started exploring Arkasin.

There is a sculpture of a man here, buried halfway in the ground with his mouth gaping open in a silent scream. There is a brownish crust in two stripes down his body, as though there was something leaking from his eyes.
There is an odd gurgling noise. From down the tunnel, there is a slight rush of air, a little fresher than you would expect. It seems you are not far from an exit.
You pour the foul-smelling fluid into the mouth of the statue. A moment later, it starts to weep out of the statue's eyes in a thick, slow-moving stream.
It is difficult to get a solid grip on the thing with all of the crust and slime interfering. Perhaps another attempt would prove more fruitful.
Looks like the remains of a traveller. He did not fare well.
The crate is full of paper and charcoal, probably meant to be sold or bartered. It is thoroughly spoiled with foul-smelling secretions from the floor and walls.
The slime of this place has done quite a number on this chest, covering the whole thing with a dull, yellow crust. It'll take some forcing to get it open.
There are a few articles of clothing in this sack. Most of it is soaked with the slime that covers everything else, but you do find what appears to be a bundle of linen.
This satchel is full of rancid foodstuffs. They are clearly inedible, but there is an intact, sealed flask of wine tucked into the corner.
With a heave and a grunt and a crunching noise, the crust gives way and the chest opens, revealing what looks like a valuable drinking set with two different kinds of liquor.
You carefully peel the slime-soaked linen away and find an unspoiled pair of fur boots. They are very nicely made, and were probably intended as trade goods.
Maybe now that they've worked it out of their systems, you can focus on stopping Vankan before he destroys the island.
The smell is reminiscent of the fluid you found when you stuffed your face while exploring Arpa.
The thrumming of Arpa's pulse and the shifting of its walls make for a long, nauseating hour, but eventually Grant and Byrne return to you, both damp with sweat and exhausted.
You can't see what's going on, but every now and then you hear what you assume is an echo of Byrne's voice down the corridor.
As you are returning the book, something else on the shelf catches your eye, something that looks like it doesn't belong there.
Gobble...
It seems your host dropped something as he left.
It suggests that the train has an on-board library. Perhaps more information could be located there.
Snap...
Snarf...
There are a few leaflets here that are still in good enough shape to be legible.
There is a book that talks about the history of the Royal Transit System. It seems a bit long.
There is a key sitting forgotten on this table.
There is a trip planning guide here that appears to still be legible.
There is little left but scraps of cloth on this mouldering corpse.
There is nothing further of use on this corpse.
These leaflets are not in good condition. They've been heavily damaged by moisture, and are only partly legible.
This crate appears to contain a number of very old bottles. You find one that still has a tight seal on its cork.
This leaflet appears to contain some historical information about the "Royal Transit System", but it is hard to piece much of it together.

Though the corpse is draped in nothing but rotting scraps of cloth, its hand is still tightly clutching a small metal object. Prying it loose, you find a small gold ring, still sparkling beneath its layer of greasy dirt.
"What have you got there, now? "The Sumptuous Garden"? I've never heard of this book. Let's see..."

An orc woman retains this legal immunity for as long as she is capable of and willing to have more children. Any orc woman who has raised two daughters to adulthood shall enjoy this immunity for the rest of her life, regardless of her childbearing choices.
An orc woman who has not yet raised two daughters and who is not currently raising a daughter who willfully destroys her ability to have children shall suffer death as punishment.
An orc woman who has not yet raised two daughters shall be prohibited from engaging in any profession which prevents her from having children, or which presents a great risk of injury to her person.
Any boy or man whose actions directly or indirectly cause a woman to suffer death or damage to her ability to bear children shall suffer death as punishment.

Any orc woman who is capable of producing children is granted immunity to any legal reprimand that could influence her ability to produce or raise said children. This includes, but is not limited to, incarceration, execution, and most forms of capital punishment.

Due to the fact that birth rates of girls are very low in orcs, and the female portion of the population is only about ten percent, there are special provisions for protecting women and girls, even from the application of the law.
Give him your copy of "The Sumptuous Garden"?
In all such cases, an orc man must serve the punishment in proxy. The man selected will be one deemed important to the woman, so as best to punish her for the indicted offense.

In order to facilitate the birth of girls, any male children may at the mother's option be surrendered, permanently and without penalty, to military training schools where they will be raised to be productive members of Orc society. A monetary compensation will be provided to the mother for children surrendered in this fashion.

In response to the contentious issue of Glamig's responsibility for the Burntfoot March, an orc named Luc Beauregard was sentenced in proxy. Most people were insulted by this gesture - he was largely unknown and thus deemed to be of minimal worth to the Queen, and the fact that a proxy was given was a tacit admission of guilt.
It is widely agreed that Glamig's decision to purge the beplagued township was shortsighted, and that the responsibility falls on her, but the question of how to deal with this is hotly debated.

One party calls for her head, saying that only the Queen's execution can possibly atone for all the deaths she has caused, but another party, mainly proponents of traditional orcish laws, argue that Spartill must serve her punishment in proxy.

Spartill is popular with both parties, and is clearly not responsible for the issues at hand. The arguments put forth for both sides are passionate and heated. Accusations of racism are levied against both sides, with the human-led party calling for the Queen's death and the Orc-led party calling for the death of Spartill.

The author of these missives also details a dramatic increase of disappearances at sea, with the tides growing progressively less hospitable. The author speculates that Tsarath is somehow responsible for this, but fails to explain exactly how.

The book says that Queen Glamig ordered a quarantine and a purge of the township. This decision was controversial, but the plague was contained, and the death toll was apparently minimal in comparison to the first plague.

The pamphlet goes on to mention that several prominent tailors have already begun vying for the prestigious honour of designing Her Royal Majesty's wedding dress. There are several flattering drawings of orc women wearing elaborate gowns, as the author hypothesizes on these tailors' trademark styles and what their gowns might look like.

The populace became restless, and Queen Glamig Cosova was eventually beaten to death by an angry mob that arose in the capital. Many assumed that Spartill would arise to fill her position, but he had disappeared entirely, and the nations of Tsarath and Crest were now flooding in, both trying to gain power in the unrest.
There is conjecture that this fact is quite vexing for other nations who would like to seize Lukatt's strategic position as a crossroads of several profitable trade routes.
This book appears to have transcripts of arguments held in the capital courts over how to appease the public for the events of The Burntfoot March.

This book details a series of historic naval battles. Most of the accounts are sterile and matter-of-fact, but there is a proud declaration that Lukatt's navy is never defeated in their home waters, and judging by the records here, that appears to be true.

This book details the discovery of a plague outbreak in a small peat-mining township at the foot of the blackglass mountains. There had been another plague some thirty years prior, so many people still had vivid memories of the suffering it caused, and were scared of what a second plague could do to them.
This book details the way in which traditional orcish law is applied differently to men and women.

This book is detailing monetary losses and death counts. During the purge, fires spread to the peat mines and ignited them. This resulted in the destruction of the island's primary source of peat, the release of toxic gasses from deep underground, and an unpredictable wildfire that ran the breadth of the Knightwood forest.
This is not a formal printing so much as the ravings of a frantic author. He is detailing the beginning of a civil war on Lukatt.

This pamphlet follows the announcement of Queen Glamig Cosova's betrothal to the popular war hero, Maxim Spartill. According to the pamphlet, the engagement is much-celebrated, as Spartill is well-loved with a long list of commendations and accomplishments.

Thousands of people lost their lives or their homes to the fires directly, and thousands more fell to banditry, overcrowding, and exposure. The overall death count in the aftermath of what the author calls "The Burntfoot March" is much, much higher than the death count of both plagues combined.
Vankan flips open to the middle of the book and reads a passage.
A bright blue light radiates out from between the planks and hinges of this wooden box.
A dark red ruby sits inside the drawer. Do you want to take it with you?
A pile of ash sits inside the fireplace.
A stifling, oppressive air begins to invade your senses as you look upward.
As you reach the top of the stairs, your head and chest begin to feel heavy and thick. The room lurches.
As you reach the top of the stairs, your head and chest begin to feel heavy and thick. You take a moment to regain your balance.
At the bottom, you can see a room which is considerably larger than the circumference of the well.
Climb back up?
Climb down?
Head upstairs?
Head upstaris?
It looks like a bit of a squeeze, but it should now be safe to enter the well.
It would be possible to climb into the well safely with the rope. Would you like to use it?
It's quite a long drop. You might be able to make it safely if you had a rope.
Most of the food here is either stale or mouldy. You comb over the table and pick out some of the least non-edible morsels.
Now that you're looking for it, you manage to find a length of rope that still seems tough enough to use for climbing.
Read the next entry?
Show the Serenity Gem to the skeleton?
Take the gem with you?
The cabinet is filled with neatly folded napkins and assorted cutlery.
The door slams shut behind you. Welcome home.
The gem you retrieved from the well is reacting strongly to the skeleton. It is pulsing with light and energy.
The journey back up is significantly harder than it was going down...
The memories of a thousand loaves of freshly baked bread are deeply ingrained in these bricks.
The mysterious forces inside the estate will not allow you to leave.
The oppressive air inside this room begins to seep into your subconscious. You don't know how much longer you can take it.
The remaining pages are blank.
The resistance suddenly gives way. The handle jolts upwards and sets into place.
The rope dangles from above, about a foot from the floor.
The skeleton begins to writhe. A wicked force knocks the gem out of your hand.
The trough is empty. The wooden boards that formed the bottom are now parted, and you can see down into the well.
The water pump is weathered and rusty, but still looks useable. Do you want to give it a try?
There is a blackened, iron key hidden underneath the mattress. The tag around the handle has the word "Cellar" written on it.
There is a leather bound diary on this desk. Would you like to read it?
There is a little key on the table. The tag attached to the handle has the word "Pantry" written on it.
There is a small splash from the previously drained water as you land. The air down here is cool and dry.
There is a stack of papers on the table. All of them have lists and arrangements for a "Summer Festival".
This bed is undressed, but still looks very comfortable.
This box is packed with camping and hiking equipment.
This trough is filled with stale water. It looks remarkably like a well.
Would you like to take the rope?
You attempt to light the lantern, but nothing happens.
You attempt to light the lantern, but your arms suddenly feel as if they are made of lead.
You begin to work the pump. Raising the handle is proving more difficult than expected.
You can feel the souls that linger on the estate gather before you.
You can see the back garden from here.
You can see the back garden from here. A chilly breeze brushes against you.
You fasten one end of the rope around the base of the water pump. After checking to see if it is secure, you drop the other end into the well.
You feel the oppressive air inside this room trying to seep into your subconscious.
You notice the bottom of the trough is lined with wooden boards, and they appear to be slightly below ground level.
You peek inside and see a large, glowing gem resting on a cushion. Looking at the gem makes you feel rested and at ease.
You take a hold of the rope and carefully climb down into the well.
You take the gem and hold it out. The skeleton is bathed in its light.

"Are you also fond of "wall-of-meat" barbarian types? I could tell. You must ensure that no matter what happens, that orc is never, ever allowed to wear a shirt. Write it into law if you must. Ensure that this one survives, will you? I couldn't bear to see him damaged."

Barrod cradles Leviathan's head in his arms, whispering softly to him and stroking his beard, like a parent consoling a wounded child. Barrod catches your gaze, and gives you a silent, appreciative nod.
Barrod disappears, and Leviathan stirs, finally speaking with a voice as deep and profound as the sea.
Beauregard balls his fists and grinds his teeth in anger for a long moment.
Even so, these pages are badly damaged. They are legible, but they crumble as you turn them. You can only read this once.
It looks as though this wall panel is fit improperly. You might be able to move it with enough brute strength.
It's heavier than it seems. You might want to catch your breath and try again.
Leviathan bows his head to you and then slips beneath the water and out of sight. It is finally over.
Lighting the incense will heal one person fully, but you will not be able to use it more than once.
Out of the brine rises the head and torso of Leviathan, at once bursting with power and helplessly restrained. His eyes, perhaps once intelligent, are glazed with impotent rage.
The doors close behind you as you step into the opulent structure. There is no going back now.
The final anchor snaps, and Leviathan pauses in his assault, his body visibly relaxing.
There is a sigil on the floor, lit in glittering silver dust and ringed with unburnt cones of incense. When you step inside, an aura of serene calm washes over you.
This corpse has been here long enough that it's hardened and turned black. Strangely, the moisture hasn't destroyed it.
This is written in a large, unsteady hand, across many pages. Whoever did this wanted to ensure that his writing survived the passage of time.
With a final, decisive strike, Leviathan's body goes limp, and he slips down into the pool, clouds of his divine blood murking the water. The battle is over.
With a mighty heave, you force the panel aside, revealing a rough-hewn passageway.
It appears that the way forward is now open.
The path to the exit is now clear.
This bow is crafted from the same strange material as the rest of this place, and touching the string runs a shiver down your spine.
This chest is thrumming with power, and your fingertips tingle when you touch the lid. Will you open it?
You decide to wait a moment before opening the chest.
A small crate has been left behind here. It's mostly full of rags, but at the bottom, you find what appears to be a potion.
Cut yourself on the blade?
The barricade doesn't move, but you could always try it again.
There is a small blade mounted at the top of this statue, with an inscription that reads, "Blood for Power".
This barricade seems fairly sturdy, but someone with a strong back might be able to tear it down.
You heave the beams out of place and the barricade topples down.
There is a note on the table here. It appears to show a list of a merchant's expenses and profits. There is a very colorfully-worded complaint about a 10,000$ expense listed at the bottom.
Everyone appears to be well-rested, and Vankan seems to be in a particularly good mood. Last night's conversation was probably a load off of his mind.
Everyone appears to have rested well.
Grinning, you tiptoe toward the door, careful not to wake your other companions.
In the morning, it appears that your party has rested well.
It is clear that he has next to no experience in this, but his fondness for you shines through, and he follows your example.
Looking around, it appears that Vankan has gone missing. His clothes are still on the floor beside his bed. Could he have written the note?
The beds are more or less clean, and the place even has a modest stock of preserves, so for once your evening is relaxed and easy.
Vankan is extremely awkward, but he gradually relaxes and begins to enjoy himself as you partake of each others' bodies in the warm evening air.
Vankan probably just went to relieve himself. The note may have been referring to waking in the morning anyway. You decide to go back to sleep.
Vankan smiles and bows his head a little when you catch his eye. It seems he's in a good mood.
When you've both finished, you return to the rest stop together and crawl back into your beds, drifting off with little trouble.
You and your party make yourselves at home in the rest stop, reassured by Vankan's predictions.
You fall asleep readily, but you wake up in the middle of the night, suddenly aware of an object in your hand. It appears to be a crumpled wad of paper.
You get back to sleep with little difficulty, and the night passes without further incident.
You make long eye contact with Vankan a few times, but he seems confused.
You rub the sleep out of your eyes and stumble out of bed, finding a spot with enough moonlight streaming in to read by.
You thought to show him the note so you could ask him about it, but it isn't anywhere to be found. Perhaps you dreamt the whole thing after all.
A sensation of panic crawls up your spine. The force that holds this place in perfect stillness is beginning to slip away, and something desperate is taking its place.
Glamig's crown begins to emit a low harmonic tone. It is resonating with something here.
Powerful magic pulses through this crystal. It appears to be the source of the strange aura that pervades this place.
The Orc reels for a moment, barely able to stand as a wave of dizziness overcomes him.
The air goes cold, and a voice like cracking ice tears through it like a shiver.
The crystal shatters as the energies that fuel it destabilize and disperse.
The lid of this chest refuses to budge even a little, as though some tremendous force is holding it shut.
This orc stands motionless in the light of the thrumming crystal. He is not breathing, but otherwise appears to be alive.
Try as you might, you cannot light this brazier. It is as if the oil is refusing the acknowledge the spark.
You relay what little information you were given by Queen Glamig, and his face goes somber.
...but it don't feel like that at all, and I can't stop thinkin' about him. I think I might actually be glad to be here.
...come by again. I guess this might become a thing. I thought it would feel weirder, like I'd done something awful, like I'd want to barf and off myself...
...it's been six years since I've been shipped out and I ain't so much as caught sight of a woman. Plus, the foreman's been real good to me and the others.
And here, this is the key he mentioned. I still have my copy. Maybe it'll come in handy.
Anyway, thanks. I'm going to see if there's any food or water to be snatched up and then be off. I'll leave the valuables for you.
Giving it a thorough check, you find a key hidden under one of the edges.
Hopelessly curious, you turn the page and keep reading.
I had to pretend I was sick today so the others wouldn't ask why I can barely walk. Holy shit I needed that. I think I still need it. He let me keep the key so I can...
I hope you don't mind, but I'm going to keep this diary. Please, it would mean a lot to me.
It looks like the entry keeps going.
It looks like there are no more loose items in the pages.
Krade... I never knew you kept a diary.
The foreman gave me the key to his cabin so I can come by quietly after dark. I've never been with an orc before, or a man either for that matter, but...
The ground near this rock is scraped, as though it's been moved recently.
There is a diary on this night table. It appears to be somewhat lurid.
They caught me sneakin' around. Figured you'd have to be a complete moron to get caught by a bunch of ogres. Guess that makes me the moron, huh?
This chest is rusted shut, and no key in the world is going to open it. Would you like to try forcing it?
Well, that sounded messy. Good to see that it's old gorgeous on the floor instead of you.
You leave the chest alone for now.
You pick an entry toward the end and start reading.
You shake the diary and a key falls out.
You turn the page, only to find it blank. You put the book back.
You've read quite enough. You put the book back where you found it.
A dryad is rooted here in front of the door. She appears to be weeping.
A kindly woman's voice echoes through the room.
A stern man's voice echoes through the room.
